dedupe_keys.name: climate risk stress testing in california geospatial framework for banks and climate exposed sectors 2026

description: This short working paper proposes a geospatial framework for climate risk stress testing in California, aimed at banks and at sectors exposed to climate hazards such as agriculture, real estate and tourism. It combines physical hazard mapping, sector-specific exposure analysis and scenario-based financial risk assessment to judge how wildfires, drought, flooding, extreme heat and transition risks could affect regional economic activity and financial stability, and it adds a survey-based implementation guide for benchmarking current climate risk practice and data needs among industry and academic stakeholders. It was written by Satya Narayana Panda and Aishworzo Saha and posted on arXiv on 17 April 2026 as a seven-page paper with one table. Coverage is California. The preprint is available free online; only the arXiv licence link is shown. Caveats: it is a framework and guide, not a completed quantitative assessment, it has not been peer reviewed, and no data or code are linked. For simulation it lays out how hazard layers, sector exposures and loan portfolios can be chained in regional climate stress scenarios for the financial system. It is related to the ECB investment fund network contagion climate stress test record in this catalogue.
